studies.title: Ketamine and other potential glutamate antidepressants.

lead: Coluracetam (also MKC-231 or BCI-540) is an experimental racetam-class compound promoted as a nootropic. It was developed by Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma, first for Alzheimer's disease, and later licensed to BrainCells Inc. for major depressive disorder and comorbid anxiety.[1][2] It is not approved anywhere.

Its best-described action is enhancement of high-affinity choline uptake, a step in acetylcholine synthesis, shown in rodent models of cholinergic deficit.[1][2] Sources examined do not link it to physical appearance.
infobox: Mitsubishi Tanabe Pharma; later BrainCells Inc.[1]
Experimental, not approved; Schedule 4 in Australia[1]

paras: Coluracetam enhances high-affinity choline uptake in rat hippocampal tissue treated with the cholinergic neurotoxin AF64A.[2] Later cell-line work reported that direct modulation of the choline transporter could not be reproduced under basal conditions, and an AMPA receptor-related action has been suggested.[2]

Mitsubishi Tanabe's Alzheimer's programme reportedly did not reach its trial endpoints.[1] A phase IIa exploratory trial under BrainCells in people with major depression and anxiety was reported to give preliminary positive signals; development was later discontinued.[1][2] Detailed published results were not located. No study has examined appearance outcomes.
It is sold online as a nootropic. Wikipedia records unverified user reports of enhanced colour perception and improved mood.[1] It is prescription-only in Australia and unapproved by the FDA.[1]

timeline.event: First synthesised by Mitsubishi Tanabe, per Grokipedia.[2]
Licensed to BrainCells Inc. for depression and anxiety.[2]
